source_title: A seesaw effect in the cryptocurrency market: Understanding the return cross predictability of cryptocurrencies
hypothesis: Recent returns of the point-in-time most-liquid large-coin basket negatively predict the next-block return of smaller eligible Binance perpetuals.
mechanism: Large cryptocurrencies lead information and capital flows; the source documents a negative intraday lead-lag from large coins to smaller coins.
signal: Negative equal-weight prior-block return of the point-in-time top-5 assets by lagged trailing 30-day dollar volume.
universe: Point-in-time assets with 30 days exact hourly continuity. Top 5 by lagged trailing 30-day close*volume are leaders; all remaining eligible assets are followers; minimum 5 leaders and 6 followers.
rebalance: Non-overlapping UTC blocks aligned to each horizon. Signal uses closes through the prior completed hour; execution uses current block open.
construction: Directional equal-weight follower basket: long followers when prior leader-basket return is negative, short followers when it is positive; gross exposure 1.0.
development_gate: canonical Spearman correlation(signal, next follower-basket return) >= 0.02, HAC p < 0.05, and positive mean signed follower return
limitations: The source uses a broader exchange universe and LASSO cross-predictability. This is a simple source-motivated falsification using the available 19-asset Binance perpetual panel, not an exact replication.
